asOf: Weekend — Sat, Jul 25, 1:00 PM PT (using Fri 7/24 close + Sat Dow fut drift)
headline: Cautious risk-off lean into the weekend: Fri close was mixed (SPX +0.05% / NDX -1.15% / DJIA +0.46%) on the second straight weekly S&P loss, AI-capex repricing still pressuring semis (MU -7%, AVGO -2.7%, SOX -5.5%) after the $797B Mag7 wipeout Thursday, new 10-12.5% Section 301 tariffs live, and Brent off $100 to $96.78 — but oil/yield relief and a +0.38% Sat Dow-fut drift hint the flush may have one leg left to the upside.

sentiment.reason: Defensive rotation winning on the day (XLU +0.22%, XLP +1.11%, XLRE +2.23% all green, semis -5.5% leading losers) but breadth only 8-of-11 sectors green and NDX -1.15% confirms growth is still being repriced; yields eased (10Y -3bp to 4.69%) and oil cooled, but fresh tariffs + Iran/Hormuz tail risk keep the tape one headline away from a re-test of 7,400.

movers.reason: Micron led the AI-capex repricing as memory exposure to hyperscaler spend got marked down after Alphabet's raised capex guide; SOX -5.5% on the day dragged the name to the bottom of the Mag7-adjacent tape.

Intel posted a blowout Q (revenue $16.1B +25%, EPS $0.42 nearly double, Data Center/AI +59%, Q3 guide raised), spiked to ~$110 after-hours then REVERSED red into the close near $100 — the cleanest sell-the-news tell of the week.

Broadcom fell with the rest of the AI-custom-silicon complex as investors questioned whether 2026/27 capex orders justify current multiples; semis -5.5% on the day (XSD) put AVGO squarely in the AI-capex-fear bucket.

news.headline: Section 301 tariffs take effect overnight: 10-12.5% on 99.4% of US imports (energy exempted)
news.context: Built to survive legal challenges, the new duties are the freshest macro overhang and land directly on a defensive tape — sector dispersion (XLY +0.6% but TSLA -7% wk) shows the market is already pricing which supply chains lose first.

news.headline: Mag7 erased $797B Thursday — worst day since April 2025 — on Alphabet capex raise + Tesla miss
news.context: The AI narrative flipped from 'promise' to 'bill' in one session; semis bled (MU -7%, SOX -5.5%) and growth multiples are now being discounted by a 4.69% 10Y, the highest discount rate since June.

news.headline: Brent crude -3.9% to $96.78 after tagging $100 Thursday on Iran/Strait of Hormuz fears
news.context: Oil cooling is the one genuine relief in the mix — takes pressure off the inflation/yield story and lets XLE (+0.40% Fri, +3.36% wk) keep its relative-strength bid without breaking the broader tape.

news.headline: Intel posts a blowout Q ($16.1B rev, EPS $0.42, Data Center/AI +59%, guide raised) then REVERSES to red
news.context: When a print this clean fades pre-market and closes lower, sentiment — not fundamentals — is running the tape; AmEx ($4.53 EPS beat, $AXP -1.4%) confirmed the pattern, marking the cleanest risk-off tell of the week.

news.headline: Spot BTC ETF outflows hit -$225M on Friday; BTC drifts to ~$65,400
news.context: Crypto is leaking into the weekend alongside the equity tape; with 10Y at 4.69% and the Mag7 bid gone, the marginal risk-asset bid has thinned — watch Monday's ETF flow print for whether $65K holds.

options.thesis: NDX -1.15% with the AI-capex fear still in charge; 7-day put/call skew steepening as hedges get bought after the Thursday wipeout
options.signal: Aug 600P / 575P put spread for continued downside beta, IV rank elevated (~58); sell the 595-600 vs. buy 575 ratio on any gap-up open

options.thesis: SPX +0.05% masking a 2nd straight weekly loss and 7,400/7,443 as the line to defend; dealer gamma still long above 7,443 but flipping short below
options.signal: 742P (0DTE Mon) on a failed 7,443 reclaim; watch 750C as the magnet if the weekend Iran/tariff tape lets futures gap higher

options.thesis: TSLA drag was the second leg of the Mag7 rout (after the Q miss + capex concerns); vol still elevated into next print, term structure steep
options.signal: Aug 280/300 call spread for mean-reversion if 280 support holds; 240P hedge against a Hormuz/tariff gap-down Monday open

options.thesis: Surprise #1 — NVDA took the AI-capex repricing on the chin alongside MU/AVGO, but with semis -5.5% on the day the IV is a buy for those who think the Alphabet capex read-through is overdone
options.signal: Sep 150P / 135P put spread (IV rank ~62) to fade post-earnings vol; or Sep 175C if 145 holds into Aug — high-conviction mean-reversion in the AI-complex's flagship

options.thesis: Surprise #2 — XLE +0.40% Fri / +3.36% wk as Brent's $100 tag pulled energy back into leadership, but crude has cooled to $96.78; relative-strength trade in a defensive tape
options.signal: XLE 95/100 call spread (Aug) into any Iran headline re-escalation; sell 90P against it to fund — pairs well with SPY 742P downside hedge

takeaway: Fri's close was a yellow-light: SPX +0.05% / NDX -1.15% with semis -5.5% leading losers but 8-of-11 sectors green, oil/yield relief on the table, and Dow futs +0.38% into the weekend. The Mag7 wipeout Thursday + live 10-12.5% tariffs + Iran/Hormuz tail risk argue against chasing the bounce, but the flush in AI-capex names (MU -7%, AVGO -2.7%) and the clean sell-the-news in INTC may be the better entries if 7,443 reclaims early Monday. Bias: neutral-to-cautious long, hedges on.

movers.reason: Q2 EPS miss but revenue beat + CEO flags 'meaningful order-count growth' in delivery + takeout; consumer-discretionary beat validates the bid into earnings week.

Hut 8 signs 15-year $9.8B lease with existing customer, fully commercializing its 1GW Beacon Point data-center in Texas — AI compute-infrastructure deal validates Hut's pivot from pure mining to AI-host.
Qwen3.8 Max preview positions Alibaba as the 'second only to Anthropic's Fable 5' frontier model — Chinese AI re-rates on the heels of Moonshot's Kimi K3 launch.

news.context: CENTCOM hitting Iranian military + 'under-construction' Darquoin power plant; third US service-member death confirmed. Iran warns of 'appropriate measures' — Hormuz tanker-flow risk keeps the crude bid live into Monday's reopen.

options.signal: Long SPY 7,450/7,350 put spreads (Jul 24) funded by short 7,650 calls — risk-reversal for Iran/mega-cap-print tail.

options.thesis: Wed Q2 print is the binary — IV rank elevated (~58%), straddle priced for ~7% move. FSD v13/Robotaxi narrative + delivery unit-economics the swing factors. Pre-earnings flow two-way.
options.signal: Sell TSLA weekly straddle (~290) into Tue close; vol crush favors sellers ahead of the print. Take profit before Wed 4 PM.

options.signal: Long MU Aug 175/200 call spread (~$3.20); cheap convexity into Wed mega-cap prints, defined-risk into memory-cycle re-pricing.

options.thesis: Surprise pick — +12% on $9.8B/15-yr data-center lease, fully commercializes 1GW Beacon Point TX. IV expanding fast off single-name news catalyst, dealer flow one-way bullish.
options.signal: Long HUT Aug 32/40 call spread (~$2.10); cheap convexity on the AI-host pivot, defined-risk into Q2 print (Aug 7).

takeaway: Pre-mkt risk-on relief-rally: semis bouncing off Fri's -10% week (SOX bear-market) on Goldman oversold-call + SK Hynix validation, mega-cap earnings week loaded (Wed = TSLA/GOOGL, Thu = INTC). Iran 9th-strike tail keeps WTI bid ($82) but Brent $90 already priced; 10Y sticky at 4.55% caps the duration-trade. Trade: sell QQQ/TSLA vol into Wed print, hedge with SPY put spreads for Iran/mega-cap tail, ride MU/HUT as single-name AI-memory/compute re-pricing. Don't trust the calm — VIX easing 9% into a binary stack is the cleanest fragile signal in the data.

options.signal: Long SPY 7,550/7,450 put spreads July 17, fund with short 7,650 calls — risk-reversal for Iran/CPI/bank-print tail. Hedge-and-go for the gauntlet.

options.signal: Sell TSLA weekly straddle (~280) into CPI/bank prints; vol crush favors premium-sellers here, no edge in direction with macro binary ahead.

options.thesis: Iran 3rd-wave strikes + Hormuz tanker incident = the cleanest geopolitical crude play in weeks. XLE +1.85% pre-mkt, dealer call flow accelerating on Aug 60C strikes.
options.signal: Long XLE Aug 62 calls (~$1.80) as tactical oil-position; cheap convexity into the Hormuz-risk premium. Stop below WTI $70.

options.thesis: Surprise pick — defense major bid on Iran escalation; IV still cheap (~22%) vs realized on geopolitical setups. Missile/air-defense order pipeline re-rates fast on CENTCOM strikes.
options.signal: Long LMT Aug 580/620 call spread (~$4.50); cheap convexity into the defense re-rate, IV at 22 with geopolitical premium still building.

takeaway: Risk-off open, but the bigger story is the calendar. Iran 3rd-wave strikes + oil +3.4% + 10Y to 4.59% = stagflation tilt into a triple-stack macro gauntlet: bank prints Tue, CPI Tue, plus ongoing Hormuz risk. VIX at 16.4 is the cleanest 'fragile' signal — institutions not paying for tail into a binary week. Trade: long XLE/LMT into the defense-energy bid, hedge with QQQ/SPY put spreads into CPI/banks, sell TSLA vol, fade the calm.
